cases.text: Why is my eye red and sticky? Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the clear membrane over the eye, making it red, gritty, itchy and sometimes sticky with discharge. Most cases are viral or allergic, and they settle within 1 to 2 weeks without treatment; antibiotics rarely change the course of viral cases. Gently bathe crusted lashes with cooled boiled water or saline, and bathe allergic eyes with a cool flannel. Viral pink eye clears on its own; drops only matter for bacterial or allergic variants a clinician identifies.

When does a fever become an emergency for adults? Seek medical advice for a fever above about 39.4C (103F), any fever lasting more than 3 days, or one that returns after you seemed to recover. Fever with a stiff neck or an unexplained rash can signal meningitis - that is a same-hour call. Adults on immune-suppressing medication or with chronic conditions should call a doctor earlier. A mild fever with ordinary cold symptoms in a healthy adult rarely needs anything beyond rest and fluids.

Does hot sauce cause ulcers? For most people spicy food is perfectly healthy - chili peppers even bring vitamin C and antioxidants. Hot peppers irritate an existing ulcer or bad heartburn, but they do not create ulcers - bacteria and anti-inflammatory painkillers do that. The burning feeling comes from capsaicin, which trips heat sensors in your mouth but does not burn or damage the tissue.

Why do dispatchers ask you to put the phone on speaker during CPR? For an unresponsive adult who is not breathing, make the emergency call first and put the phone on speaker so your hands stay free. The dispatcher stays on the line, confirms the steps, and can tell you where the nearest public defibrillator (AED) is. Then start chest compressions and keep going until the ambulance crew takes over, an AED is attached, or the person starts breathing normally. Doing something imperfectly is far better than doing nothing while waiting for a trained responder. First aid courses teach the full sequence and are worth taking - this guidance is awareness, not training.

Should I wake up at the same time every day? Your body clock runs on consistency: going to bed and - most importantly - waking at the same time every day trains it to make you sleepy and alert on schedule. Big weekend lie-ins feel like repayment but create 'social jet lag', leaving Monday mornings feeling like jet lag after a long flight. If you must shift, moving bedtime and wake time by 15-30 minutes at a time works far better than one dramatic reset.

How do I stop a cut from bleeding? Firm, continuous pressure with something clean is the single most effective way to stop bleeding. If you can, raise the injured part above the level of the heart to slow the blood flow. Lifting the cloth early is the most common reason bleeding seems to never stop. Once it has stopped, keep a clean dressing on it for support and protection.

Is breakfast the most important meal of the day? Breakfast is a useful meal for many people - it is a chance for fiber and protein, and children tend to concentrate better at school when they have eaten. For adults, the evidence on weight is mixed: some studies favor breakfast eaters, others find little difference. If you skip breakfast and feel fine, that is a reasonable choice; if you raid the snack drawer mid-morning, a balanced breakfast may steady you.

There is dust in my eye - how do I get it out? Rubbing can turn a speck into a corneal scratch, which is far worse than the speck. If blinking does not work, rinse the eye with clean lukewarm water or saline - tilt the head so the water runs from the inner corner outward. Never try to remove anything embedded in the eye: cover it loosely (a paper cup works) and get emergency help. See a doctor urgently for pain that does not settle, vision changes, or sensitivity to light after any eye injury.

What causes sudden dizziness? Brief lightheadedness on standing is usually a short blood-pressure dip, made more likely by dehydration, heat, hunger or certain medications. Vertigo - the sensation that you or the room is spinning - points to the inner ear, where the balance organs live. Sitting or lying down promptly prevents the dizziness from becoming a faint. Recurrent episodes, or dizziness on turning over in bed with brief spins, are worth describing to a doctor - the inner-ear causes are often very treatable.

Can walking help me lose weight? Brisk walking counts fully toward moderate activity guidelines and meaningfully lowers the risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes and depression. It is the most accessible form of exercise: no equipment, no skill, low injury risk, and it can be chopped into small pieces across the day. Brisk means you feel warmer and breathe harder but can still talk - roughly 100 steps a minute is a common benchmark. Because it is sustainable, walking is the exercise most people actually keep doing, which matters more than any theoretical better option.

My grandmother fainted and was confused afterward - is that normal? Lay the person down and raise their legs above heart level to send blood back to the brain, and loosen tight collars or belts. Most people wake within a minute or two and feel washed out but otherwise fine. Do not crowd them, splash water or prop them sitting up straight away. Call emergency services if they do not recover quickly, are confused afterward, fainted during exercise or with chest pain, are pregnant or older with other conditions, or if they hit their head falling. Once recovered, getting up slowly and having a drink and a snack helps prevent a repeat.

Why do doctors recommend walking so much? Brisk walking counts fully toward moderate activity guidelines and meaningfully lowers the risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes and depression. It is the most accessible form of exercise: no equipment, no skill, low injury risk, and it can be chopped into small pieces across the day. The 'brisk' bar is simple: noticeably faster breathing, still able to chat. Because it is sustainable, walking is the exercise most people actually keep doing, which matters more than any theoretical better option. A 10-minute walk after meals is a genuinely evidence-backed habit for blood sugar and mood.

What does a spacer do? Reliever inhalers (usually blue) contain fast-acting medicine that opens the airways within minutes - they are the emergency tool. Preventer inhalers contain a low steroid dose taken every day whether or not you feel symptoms, because they work by calming the underlying inflammation. Skipping the preventer while using the reliever more and more is the classic pattern that ends in an asthma attack. A spacer tube makes inhalers more effective - much more medicine reaches the lungs, especially in children - and a pharmacist or nurse can check your technique anytime. Rinse the mouth after using a steroid preventer to avoid throat irritation and thrush.

What is more important for weight loss - diet or exercise? Lasting weight loss comes from a small, steady calorie gap: smaller portions, more fiber and protein, fewer sugary drinks and less alcohol, plus more daily movement. The diets that keep weight off are ones you could still be following in five years; extreme rules almost always bounce back. Fad diets work briefly because they cut calories, but most people regain the weight when they stop - changes you can live with win.

What should I eat for breakfast to stay full until lunch? Build breakfast around fiber plus protein - for example oatmeal with berries and nuts, or eggs with wholegrain toast. Sugary cereal or pastries spike your blood sugar and leave you hungry again within a couple of hours. Short on time? Overnight oats made the night before, a banana with peanut butter, or wholegrain toast all travel well.

Why do I get headaches at my desk? Tension headaches feel like a dull, pressing band around the head, usually on both sides, and they are the most common headache type. Stress, poor posture, screen time, skipped meals and dehydration are the usual triggers. Water, a break from screens, stretching neck and shoulders, and a simple painkiller like paracetamol or ibuprofen usually settle one. Painkillers more than about 10 days a month can themselves cause rebound headaches, so use them sparingly.

What should I do with leftover antibiotics? Take antibiotics exactly as prescribed - the dose, the times, and the duration your prescriber gave - and ask them directly if you are unsure about the course length. Never share antibiotics or self-treat from leftovers: the drug may be wrong for the infection, and partial courses breed resistance. Report rashes, severe diarrhea or allergic symptoms to your doctor promptly. Some antibiotics interact with other medications, including oral contraceptives - read the leaflet. Return unused antibiotics to a pharmacy for safe disposal rather than keeping them in the cabinet.

I got shampoo in my baby's eyes - is that an emergency? Hold the eyelids open and flush the eye with clean lukewarm running water for a full 15 to 20 minutes, letting it run from the inner corner outward. Remove contact lenses as soon as flushing starts if they do not come out on their own. Call emergency services or Poison Control while or after flushing - some chemicals keep damaging tissue even after rinsing. Harsh household chemicals like drain cleaner or bleach are true eye emergencies; mild soap stings but rinses clean.

How do I know if I am not drinking enough? Early signs of dehydration include thirst, a dry mouth, and passing darker, smellier pee less often. You may also feel tired, headachy or lightheaded, and find it harder to concentrate. If your pee is dark yellow or strong-smelling, that is a clear sign to drink more. Young children and older adults can dehydrate faster than healthy adults, so keep an eye on them in hot weather.

What do I do if my burn blisters? Do not burst a burn blister on purpose - the fluid inside is sterile and the skin on top protects the raw area underneath. Cover it loosely with a clean, non-fluffy dressing instead. If it bursts on its own, wash gently with clean water, leave the flap of skin in place, and cover it with a plaster or sterile dressing. See a doctor if the area becomes increasingly red, swollen, painful, or oozes yellow-green pus.

Should children have less sugar than adults? For adults, guidance is to keep added sugar below about 30 grams a day - roughly 7 sugar cubes. Children should have less: no more than about 6 cubes a day for ages 7 to 10, and less again for younger kids. It is 'free sugars' that count against the limit: the kind added to products, plus honey, syrups and juice. Whole fruit and plain milk do not count.

Should I put oil in my ear? Most earaches, especially with a cold, are viral middle-ear infections that improve within about 3 days without antibiotics. Paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain, and holding something comfortably warm against the ear, are the mainstay of care. Do not put oil, drops or cotton buds into a painful ear unless a doctor has advised it - cotton buds mainly push wax deeper. Doctors increasingly delay antibiotics for 48 to 72 hours to see if the body clears it, precisely because most do.

What is in OTC sleep medicine? Most non-prescription sleep aids rely on sedating antihistamines, the same drowsy ingredient as in allergy medicine. After a few nights, antihistamine-based aids stop helping sleep but keep causing heavy-headed mornings. They are acceptable occasionally, but for ongoing insomnia the evidence-backed route is CBT-I and sleep habits rather than nightly pills.

What are the risks of sitting too long? Long uninterrupted sitting carries its own health risks that a single daily workout does not fully erase. Standing or moving briefly every 30 to 60 minutes - a lap of the room, a few stairs, a 2-minute stretch - measurably improves blood sugar and circulation. Set a loose timer - the movement matters more than the specific exercise you pick. The practical pattern is exercise plus frequent breaks: the two protect different systems. Meetings and calls are easy anchors: walk during calls, stand during meetings, move between tasks.

How many hours of sleep should I get a night? Most adults need between 7 and 9 hours of sleep a night to function well. A few rare people thrive on less, but studies show most people who sleep 6 hours or less are measurably impaired - and often don't notice it. A useful test: if you need an alarm plus caffeine to drag yourself up, and you crash on free weekends, you are running a sleep debt.

How do I treat a sprained ankle? Rest, wrapped ice, a compression bandage and elevation are the four first-day moves for a sprain. Ice straight on bare skin can cause cold injury, so always wrap it. Avoid heat, alcohol, running and deep massage in the first 48 to 72 hours - they can increase swelling. Gentle movement as pain allows usually speeds recovery more than total rest.

What lifestyle changes help acid reflux? Smaller portions, upright after eating, and known-trigger reduction are the evidence-backed basics. Raising the head of the bed 10 to 20 centimeters, or using a wedge pillow, reduces night-time reflux - stacking extra pillows alone just kinks the neck. Losing excess weight around the middle takes direct pressure off the stomach and often reduces reflux noticeably. Antacids neutralize acid on contact and work fast for episodes; if you need them most days for weeks, see a doctor about ongoing treatment.

How many sugar cubes a day is considered OK? For adults, guidance is to keep added sugar below about 30 grams a day - roughly 7 sugar cubes. Children should have less: no more than about 6 cubes a day for ages 7 to 10, and less again for younger kids. The limit covers sugar added to food and drinks plus honey, syrups and fruit juice - not the natural sugar in whole fruit or plain milk. Most free sugars hide in soda, candy, cookies, sweetened cereal and sauces rather than the sugar bowl.

What foods should I avoid with reflux? Smaller portions, upright after eating, and known-trigger reduction are the evidence-backed basics. Raising the head of the bed 10 to 20 centimeters, or using a wedge pillow, reduces night-time reflux - stacking extra pillows alone just kinks the neck. Losing excess weight around the middle takes direct pressure off the stomach and often reduces reflux noticeably. Antacids neutralize acid on contact and work fast for episodes; if you need them most days for weeks, see a doctor about ongoing treatment. Frequent reflux over years can change the esophageal lining, which is the reason persistent symptoms deserve review rather than a lifetime of antacids.

How do I know if a bread is really wholegrain? Whole grains keep all three parts of the grain - the bran, the germ and the starchy middle - while white flour keeps only the middle. That leaves more fiber, B vitamins, iron and magnesium in what you eat. Look for oats, whole-wheat bread, brown rice, barley and popcorn - they all count as whole grains. Check the label carefully: 'made with whole grain' can mean just a sprinkle, so 'whole grain' should be high on the ingredients list.

My elderly mother will not drink and seems confused - is that dehydration? Urgent signs include no urination for 8 or more hours, sunken eyes, extreme thirst with inability to keep fluids down, marked lethargy or confusion, and cold, mottled hands and feet. Babies and older adults dehydrate faster and can deteriorate quickly, so they cross the urgent threshold sooner than healthy adults. In babies: dry diapers, a sunken soft spot and listlessness are the red flags to act on. Confusion in an older person during a vomiting illness is dehydration until a doctor says otherwise.

When can I go back to work after a stomach bug? Alcohol hand gel does not kill norovirus well - washing with soap and warm water is the effective method, especially after the bathroom and before food. Clean surfaces (especially the bathroom, door handles and anywhere vomit landed) with a bleach-based cleaner, and wash laundry hot. The 48-hour rule exists because people shed virus for days after feeling better. Keep the sick person's towels and utensils separate where practical. Anyone cleaning up vomit should open windows, wear gloves, and use paper towels disposed of in a sealed bag.

Can my child sleep after a head bump? Big cry, then back to normal play, is reassuring - but keep checking in over the next two days. Comfort them, offer a wrapped cold pack, and let them sleep if they settle - sleeping is fine as long as they rouse normally. Watch for 48 hours for repeated vomiting, unusual drowsiness or floppiness, irritability you cannot settle, unequal pupils, or any loss of consciousness. Babies under 1, falls from a significant height, or any of those warning signs mean the child should be seen by a doctor. If anything about their behavior seems wrong to you, trust that instinct and get them checked.

Do fevers always need medicine? Keep the room comfortable and dress lightly - do not pile on blankets, and do not use ice baths or cold sponging, which cause shivering that pushes temperature back up. Cold sponging backfires - shivering generates heat and makes the fever fight you. Paracetamol or ibuprofen are for comfort when the person is miserable, not for hitting a target number. Rest as much as the body asks for while the immune system works.

How many rest days should I take a week? The workout is the stimulus; the rest day is where the improvement is manufactured. For moderate activity like walking, daily movement is fine; for hard strength or interval sessions, leave 24 to 48 hours before working the same muscles hard again. Rest days can be active - walking, stretching, easy cycling - which often reduces stiffness more than lying still. Signs you need more recovery include stalling performance, persistent fatigue, poor sleep, and irritability.

Why do I need vitamin D in winter? Vitamin D keeps bones, teeth and muscles healthy, and most of us make it when sunlight lands on our skin. In winter, when sunlight is too weak for your skin to make vitamin D, a daily 10 microgram supplement covers the gap. Food helps a little - oily fish, eggs and fortified cereals - but rarely covers what you need on its own.

How can I prevent nightmares in children? Nightmares are a normal part of childhood - most kids have them, especially between ages 3 and 8, often in the second half of the night. Reassure, keep lights low, and avoid long discussions mid-night - children take their cue from your calm. Stressful events, scary shows and poor sleep raise nightmare frequency, so a steady routine helps. If nightmares are near-nightly, involve injuries, or leave a child afraid to sleep, bring it up with a doctor.

Why can't I sleep after a night shift? Daytime sleep is lighter and shorter by nature, so blackout darkness, cool air and ear protection are doing real work, not just comfort. Keeping the same sleep block even on days off - or shifting it only slightly - beats flip-flopping between schedules. A nap before a night shift and bright light during the shift help alertness; a doctor or pharmacist can discuss melatonin timing if problems persist.

Should I rinse after brushing my teeth? Brush twice a day for about 2 minutes with fluoride toothpaste - for adults, 1350 to 1500 parts per million fluoride. Spit out the foam but do not rinse with water: leaving a thin layer of fluoride on your teeth is what strengthens enamel overnight. Once in the morning and once last thing before bed - the bedtime brush matters most, because saliva flow drops while you sleep.

When does flu treatment with antivirals work best? Antiviral medicines such as oseltamivir can shorten flu by about a day and reduce complications, but only if started within about 48 hours of the first symptoms. They are mainly recommended for people at higher risk of complications - older adults, pregnant people, and those with asthma, diabetes or heart disease. For otherwise healthy adults with mild flu, doctors often judge rest and fluids the better trade-off. If you think you have flu and fall in a risk group, call a doctor early rather than waiting to see how it develops.

Why won't the doctor give me antibiotics? Viruses cause most everyday infections - colds, most sore throats, most coughs, flu, norovirus - and they clear as your immune system does the work. Bacterial infections (strep throat, many urinary infections, some chest infections) are the ones antibiotics treat. Even then, many minor bacterial infections are handled by the immune system; antibiotics speed recovery and prevent spread in specific cases a doctor can judge. Every unnecessary antibiotic course trains bacteria to survive the next real one.

I sliced my finger on a knife and it will not stop bleeding - what do I do? Press firmly on the cut with a clean cloth or gauze and keep it there for a solid 10 minutes without peeking. If you can, raise the injured part above the level of the heart to slow the blood flow. Lifting the cloth early is the most common reason bleeding seems to never stop. Once it has stopped, keep a clean dressing on it for support and protection.

Does a white or charred burn need medical care? Get medical help for any burn larger than the person's palm, or on the face, hands, feet, genitals, or over a joint. Also seek care for burns that look white, leathery or charred (a sign all skin layers are affected), and for all chemical and electrical burns. Young children, babies and older adults should have most burns other than tiny ones assessed by a professional. While you wait, keep up the cool running water and cover the area loosely.

Why is my cough still here after the cold ended? Most colds run their course in 7 to 10 days, with symptoms peaking around days 2 to 3. A lingering cough after the stuffy nose clears is common and can last 2 to 3 weeks; it does not mean you need antibiotics. Symptoms that keep worsening after a week, or a fever that returns after you had improved, suggest something else is going on. Rest and time are genuinely the main treatment - there is no cure for the common cold. Recovery slows if you skip sleep and hydration, so rest is not optional advice - it is the treatment.

Why does my skin itch after a hot shower? The post-shower itch is evaporating water pulling more moisture from skin whose oils the hot water already stripped. Choose lukewarm water, keep showers short, and pat skin almost dry before applying moisturizer within a few minutes. That after-shower moisturizer is the step most people skip, and it makes the biggest difference in winter.

Is antibacterial soap better than regular soap? Antibacterial soap has never been shown to outperform ordinary soap and water in real-world handwashing. Regulators have found no proof that antibacterial soaps protect people better, and some ingredients in them (like triclosan) have been restricted over safety questions. Technique - 20 seconds, all surfaces, thorough drying - is what cleans hands, not the marketing on the bottle.

How hard should I be breathing during exercise? The simplest gauge is the talk test: during moderate activity you can hold a conversation but would struggle to sing. During vigorous activity you can manage only a few words at a time - think running, fast cycling, intervals, or swimming laps. Brisk walking, easy cycling on flat ground, doubles tennis and heavy cleaning are solidly moderate for most people. Intensity is relative to fitness, so a hill that is moderate for one person is vigorous for another - the talk test adapts automatically.

When is the latest I can drink coffee? Half the caffeine from your 3 pm coffee is still circulating around 8 pm - right when your body should be winding down. A mid-afternoon coffee can therefore still be working at lights-out, making it harder to fall asleep and lighter once you do. Most people sleep noticeably better if they finish caffeine by early-to-mid afternoon.

Should children have less sugar than adults? For adults, guidance is to keep added sugar below about 30 grams a day - roughly 7 sugar cubes. Children should have less: no more than about 6 cubes a day for ages 7 to 10, and less again for younger kids. It is 'free sugars' that count against the limit: the kind added to products, plus honey, syrups and juice. Whole fruit and plain milk do not count. Most free sugars hide in soda, candy, cookies, sweetened cereal and sauces rather than the sugar bowl.

Are nuts fattening? Nuts are packed with unsaturated fats, protein, fiber, vitamin E and minerals. Even though nuts are calorie-dense, a daily handful does not tend to cause weight gain - they satisfy hunger efficiently. Choose unsalted versions, and plain over honey-coated or heavily roasted. Nut butters count too, as long as the label says 100% nuts with no added sugar or palm oil.

Is a fever bad for you? Fever is a defense mechanism doing its job; the illness causing it is what needs watching. The number on the thermometer matters less than how the person looks and feels. Treating the discomfort with paracetamol or ibuprofen is reasonable; forcing a normal temperature is not required, and mild fevers may even help the immune response. How unwell someone seems - alertness, drinking, breathing - tells you more than the reading. A temperature of about 38C (100.4F) or higher counts as a fever when measured properly.

My child has a fever and purple spots - what do I do? Press a clear glass firmly against the rash: if the spots stay visible through the glass rather than fading, that is a non-blanching rash, and with fever it is a medical emergency (possible meningitis or sepsis). Painful, blistering or fast-spreading rashes are urgent dermatology territory, not home-care territory. A rash that appears after starting a new medication also warrants prompt review. Do not wait for other symptoms to develop - with sepsis, hours matter.

Do animal bites need medical attention? A cut may need professional care if it is deep, has edges that gape apart, if you can see fat or deeper tissue, or if bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure. Cuts on the face, puncture wounds, and any animal or human bite should be checked - infection and scarring risks are higher there. When in doubt, get it looked at; stitches work best within hours of the injury.

When should I go to the doctor for a minor illness? Most minor illnesses follow a predictable arc - worst in the first 2 to 3 days, clearly better by the end of the week - so it is reasonable to manage them with rest, fluids and simple remedies first. Escalate when symptoms are severe or getting worse rather than better, when a fever or symptoms last much longer than expected, or when any red-flag sign appears (breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe pain, confusion, non-fading rash). People with chronic conditions, weakened immune systems, pregnancy, or very young children should set their personal threshold lower. Pharmacists triage minor illness well and cost nothing - use them as the first step. In the US, 911 or the local emergency number is for emergencies; urgent care or a same-day appointment covers most other worrying situations.

How long is one sleep cycle? Sleep runs in cycles of roughly 90 minutes, moving through light sleep, deep sleep and REM (dream) sleep. The first half of the night is deep-sleep-heavy for body repair; the second half is REM-heavy for dreams and emotional sorting. Waking mid-cycle leaves you groggier, which is one reason a consistent schedule beats constantly shifting bedtimes.

How does an EpiPen work? Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness or collapse, and hives spreading over the whole body mean a severe allergic reaction called anaphylaxis. Call emergency services immediately - this can become life-threatening within minutes. If the person carries an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen style), use it into the outer thigh right away and hold it in place as instructed. Lay them down with legs raised if dizzy, and stay with them until help arrives; a second pen dose may be given if there is no improvement after 5 minutes and the instructions allow it.

I cut my knee on the pavement - what should I do once the bleeding stops? Once bleeding has stopped, rinse the cut under clean running water to wash out dirt - this does more good than any antiseptic. Pat the skin around it dry, leave the wound itself alone, and cover it with a plaster or sterile dressing. Alcohol and undiluted antiseptic sting and can damage healthy tissue, so keep them for the skin around the wound if at all. Change the dressing daily and keep the cut clean and dry while it heals.

How much protein do I need a day? Most adults need roughly 0.75 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight a day - about 45 grams for the average woman and 55 grams for the average man. That works out to a couple of palm-sized portions of protein foods spread across the day, and most people already eat this much without trying. Your body cannot bank spare protein as muscle - the surplus is used for energy or stored as fat.

Why does caffeine matter when you are expecting? Pregnant women are advised to keep caffeine under 200 mg a day - about 2 mugs of instant coffee or one strong filter coffee. Higher caffeine intakes are linked to a greater risk of low birth weight and miscarriage. Remember to count tea, cola, energy drinks and chocolate towards the daily total. Decaf coffee, plain tea in moderation and water are easy swaps while you are expecting.

What are the benefits of walking daily? Walking briskly is real, guideline-qualifying exercise - not a consolation prize. It is the most accessible form of exercise: no equipment, no skill, low injury risk, and it can be chopped into small pieces across the day. Brisk means you feel warmer and breathe harder but can still talk - roughly 100 steps a minute is a common benchmark. Because it is sustainable, walking is the exercise most people actually keep doing, which matters more than any theoretical better option.

Are frozen vegetables as healthy as fresh? Frozen fruit and vegetables are picked ripe and frozen within hours, so they hold on to their vitamins very well. Canned is fine too - choose fruit canned in juice rather than syrup, and vegetables with no added salt. Frozen options are often cheaper, cut food waste, and mean there is always a vegetable ready in the freezer.

I keep getting dizzy every day - should I see a doctor? Call emergency services if dizziness comes with chest pain, palpitations, new weakness or numbness, slurred speech, severe headache, or double vision - these can signal heart or brain problems. See a doctor promptly for dizziness that keeps recurring, lasts continuously for hours, or comes with new hearing loss in one ear. Dizziness from standing too fast in a warm room is usually benign; dizziness that arrives with neurological signs never gets the benign assumption. If dizziness has already caused faints, describe those events to a doctor rather than only the dizziness. New severe dizziness in someone over 65 or with cardiovascular risk factors warrants a lower threshold for checking.

How long can you go without peeing before worrying? Urgent signs include no urination for 8 or more hours, sunken eyes, extreme thirst with inability to keep fluids down, marked lethargy or confusion, and cold, mottled hands and feet. Babies and older adults dehydrate faster and can deteriorate quickly, so they cross the urgent threshold sooner than healthy adults. A baby with a sunken fontanelle (soft spot on the head), no wet diapers for hours, or crying without tears needs same-day care. Confusion in an older person during a vomiting illness is dehydration until a doctor says otherwise.

How often should I do strength training? Guidelines call for muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days a week, working all the major muscle groups: legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders and arms. Weights are one option, but bodyweight moves (squats, push-ups, lunges), resistance bands, and heavy gardening all count. Bodyweight exercises, bands and lifting everyday heavy things all qualify as strengthening. It is the half of the exercise guidelines most people skip - and the one with the steepest benefits once you start.

How can I prevent nightmares in children? Nightmares are a normal part of childhood - most kids have them, especially between ages 3 and 8, often in the second half of the night. The best response is calm comfort: a hug, reassurance that it was a dream, and back to bed; keeping the room dim and settling quietly avoids fully waking them. Stressful events, scary shows and poor sleep raise nightmare frequency, so a steady routine helps.

How long does a cold last? Most colds run their course in 7 to 10 days, with symptoms peaking around days 2 to 3. A lingering cough after the stuffy nose clears is common and can last 2 to 3 weeks; it does not mean you need antibiotics. Getting worse after day 7, or a second fever spike, is the pattern that deserves a doctor's visit. Rest and time are genuinely the main treatment - there is no cure for the common cold. Recovery slows if you skip sleep and hydration, so rest is not optional advice - it is the treatment.

Can a 5 pm coffee ruin my night? Caffeine lingers: about half of it is still in your body roughly 5 hours after you drink it. A mid-afternoon coffee can therefore still be working at lights-out, making it harder to fall asleep and lighter once you do. Most people sleep noticeably better if they finish caffeine by early-to-mid afternoon.

Can cold weather set off asthma? The most common triggers are respiratory infections, pollen and dust mites, pet dander, cold air, smoke, and exercise. Identifying your personal triggers lets you prevent flare-ups instead of just treating them - an asthma diary or app helps spot the pattern. Smoke (including vaping and secondhand) is one of the most damaging triggers and should be avoided completely. People with asthma should exercise; a warm-up and reliever nearby manage most exercise symptoms.

I got shampoo in my baby's eyes - is that an emergency? Hold the eyelids open and flush the eye with clean lukewarm running water for a full 15 to 20 minutes, letting it run from the inner corner outward. Remove contact lenses as soon as flushing starts if they do not come out on their own. Call emergency services or Poison Control while or after flushing - some chemicals keep damaging tissue even after rinsing. Everyday shampoo stings but is not a chemical emergency; industrial cleaners, drain products and acids are.

Can I take antihistamines every night for sleep? Most non-prescription sleep aids rely on sedating antihistamines, the same drowsy ingredient as in allergy medicine. After a few nights, antihistamine-based aids stop helping sleep but keep causing heavy-headed mornings. They are acceptable occasionally, but for ongoing insomnia the evidence-backed route is CBT-I and sleep habits rather than nightly pills.

Is five a day enough, or should I aim higher? The standard advice is at least 5 portions of fruit and vegetables a day, roughly 400 grams in total. Five a day is a minimum rather than a ceiling - more is generally better, and variety counts. Fresh, frozen, canned and dried all count towards the total.

Is it okay to take someone else's antibiotics? Follow the prescription exactly and check with the prescriber rather than the internet when in doubt. Never share antibiotics or self-treat from leftovers: the drug may be wrong for the infection, and partial courses breed resistance. Report rashes, severe diarrhea or allergic symptoms to your doctor promptly. Many antibiotics interact with other medicines (some affect contraceptive pills), so mention everything you take. Return unused antibiotics to a pharmacy for safe disposal rather than keeping them in the cabinet.

Do I need antibiotics for pink eye? Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the clear membrane over the eye, making it red, gritty, itchy and sometimes sticky with discharge. Most cases are viral or allergic, and they settle within 1 to 2 weeks without treatment; antibiotics rarely change the course of viral cases. Gently bathe crusted lashes with cooled boiled water or saline, and bathe allergic eyes with a cool flannel. Viral pink eye clears on its own; drops only matter for bacterial or allergic variants a clinician identifies.

How do I know if a head injury is serious? Put a wrapped cold pack on the bump for 15 to 20 minutes, then keep watch for the next 48 hours. Urgent warning signs include being knocked out even briefly, repeated vomiting, a worsening headache, unusual drowsiness or confusion, slurred speech, unequal pupil sizes, seizure, or blood or clear fluid from the ears or nose. Feeling fine right away does not rule out a delayed problem, which is why the 48-hour watch matters. Mild headache and a tender lump that slowly improve are common after minor bumps.

How long should you run a burn under cold water? Cool the burn under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 full minutes, starting as soon as you can. The water draws the heat out of the skin, which is what limits the damage. It still helps even if you start a few minutes late. Take off rings or watches near the area early, before the skin starts to swell. Cool the burn, not the whole person - keep the rest of them warm so they do not get chilled.

How long does conjunctivitis last? Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the clear membrane over the eye, making it red, gritty, itchy and sometimes sticky with discharge. Most cases are viral or allergic, and they settle within 1 to 2 weeks without treatment; antibiotics rarely change the course of viral cases. Gently bathe crusted lashes with cooled boiled water or saline, and bathe allergic eyes with a cool flannel. Stop contact lens wear until the eye has fully settled, and do not share towels or pillows.

How does the flu vaccine work? Flu viruses mutate constantly, so the vaccine is reformulated each year to match the strains expected to circulate. Annual vaccination also keeps your immunity topped up, which fades over months. A sore arm and a day of mild achiness is your immune system responding - it is not influenza. Even when it does not prevent infection entirely, it reduces severity, complications and spread; autumn is the usual best timing.

How do I know if chest pain is a heart attack? Call emergency services immediately for chest pain or pressure that lasts more than a few minutes, especially with sweating, nausea, shortness of breath or pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back. Wait for the ambulance rather than driving - paramedics can start treatment on the spot. Have the person sit down, stay calm and stop all exertion while help is coming. Heart attack pain is not always severe or classic; pressure, tightness or indigestion-like discomfort in a high-risk person deserves the same emergency call. Emergency services may advise chewing an aspirin while help is on the way - only follow their instruction.

Is 150 minutes of exercise really necessary? The standard guideline is at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity a week, or 75 minutes of vigorous activity, or a mix of the two. Spreading it over most days works better than one giant session - even 20 to 30 minutes on 5 days clears the bar. Weekend-warrior patterns still beat nothing, but spreading activity lowers injury risk and keeps energy steadier. Adults should add muscle-strengthening work on at least 2 days a week on top of the minutes.

Why do we get fevers when we are sick? A fever is your immune system turning up body temperature to help fight infection - it is a response, not a disease. The number on the thermometer matters less than how the person looks and feels. Treating the discomfort with paracetamol or ibuprofen is reasonable; forcing a normal temperature is not required, and mild fevers may even help the immune response. How unwell someone seems - alertness, drinking, breathing - tells you more than the reading. A temperature of about 38C (100.4F) or higher counts as a fever when measured properly.

What is the daily limit for added sugar? For adults, guidance is to keep added sugar below about 30 grams a day - roughly 7 sugar cubes. Children should have less: no more than about 6 cubes a day for ages 7 to 10, and less again for younger kids. It is 'free sugars' that count against the limit: the kind added to products, plus honey, syrups and juice. Whole fruit and plain milk do not count. Most free sugars hide in soda, candy, cookies, sweetened cereal and sauces rather than the sugar bowl.

Do I need dairy for calcium? Dairy is an easy calcium-and-protein package, but you can get the same nutrients from fortified plant drinks, leafy greens, tofu and fish with soft bones. Guidance suggests some dairy each day - for example a glass of milk, a pot of yogurt and a matchbox-sized piece of cheese. Lower-fat and lower-sugar versions deliver the same calcium with less saturated fat, and fortified plant drinks work for those who prefer them.

Should I put a burn under water right away? Cool the burn under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 full minutes, starting as soon as you can. The water draws the heat out of the skin, which is what limits the damage. It still helps even if you start a few minutes late. Take off rings or watches near the area early, before the skin starts to swell. Cool the burn, not the whole person - keep the rest of them warm so they do not get chilled.

How long should a warm-up take? Start the same activity slower and lighter, then ramp up over 5-10 minutes - that is the whole warm-up. It shifts blood to the muscles, loosens joints, and lets effort feel smoother from the first hard minute. A proper warm-up lowers the strain of sudden intense effort on heart and muscles, which matters most as you get older or less trained. Save static stretching for after; warm-up time is better spent moving. If the first minutes of exercise feel unexpectedly hard, that is usually an under-warmed body talking.

Is carrying heavy shopping bags exercise? A beginner home session can be as simple as squats to a chair, wall or knee push-ups, step-ups on a stair, and rows with a resistance band. Two rounds of 8 to 12 repetitions each, taking the sets close to fatigue, covers the guideline for that day. Effort near the last few repetitions is the signal that the muscle is being challenged enough. Everyday load-bearing - carrying groceries, hauling a vacuum upstairs, digging in the garden - counts as resistance work too. Progress by adding reps, sets or load gradually - never by jumping to heavy weights on day one.

Do I need protein shakes or supplements? Most adults need roughly 0.75 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight a day - about 45 grams for the average woman and 55 grams for the average man. That works out to a couple of palm-sized portions of protein foods spread across the day, and most people already eat this much without trying. Protein beyond what you need is not stored as extra muscle; it is burned for energy or stored as fat. People who train hard, are pregnant, or are older may benefit from a little more, and a dietitian can advise.

Should I bundle up when I have a fever? Light clothing, steady fluids and rest are the comfort basics; medicine is optional if they feel fine. Offer fluids regularly; fever increases fluid loss through sweat. Paracetamol or ibuprofen are for comfort when the person is miserable, not for hitting a target number. Rest as much as the body asks for while the immune system works.

Why is oily fish good for you? Aim for two portions of fish a week, and make one of them oily - each portion about 140 grams. Oily fish includes salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring and trout; these are rich in omega-3 fats that support heart and brain health. Pregnant women should keep oily fish to no more than two portions a week and avoid shark, swordfish and marlin because of mercury.

Is carrying heavy shopping bags exercise? A beginner home session can be as simple as squats to a chair, wall or knee push-ups, step-ups on a stair, and rows with a resistance band. Two rounds of 8 to 12 repetitions each, taking the sets close to fatigue, covers the guideline for that day. Effort near the last few repetitions is the signal that the muscle is being challenged enough. Everyday load-bearing - carrying groceries, hauling a vacuum upstairs, digging in the garden - counts as resistance work too.

Should I squeeze a splinter out? Wash your hands and the area, then grip the exposed end with clean tweezers and pull it out at the same angle it went in. If it is buried under the skin, a sterilized needle can gently lift the skin over the end before you tweeze it out. Wash the area again afterward, cover it, and watch for redness or pus over the next few days. Do not dig aggressively; splinters that are deep, near the eye, or causing spreading redness belong with a doctor, and a deep dirty splinter may raise the tetanus question.

How do I avoid trans fats? Trans fats are the unhealthiest fats there are - worse than saturated fat - which is why most countries have banned artificial ones. Many countries have now banned or restricted them, so they are far less common than they used to be. Check labels for 'partially hydrogenated oil', and go easy on hard margarines, deep-fried takeout and packaged baked goods.

How long should a home strength workout be? A beginner home session can be as simple as squats to a chair, wall or knee push-ups, step-ups on a stair, and rows with a resistance band. Two rounds of 8 to 12 repetitions each, taking the sets close to fatigue, covers the guideline for that day. Ten to fifteen focused minutes is genuinely enough when done twice a week with effort. Everyday load-bearing - carrying groceries, hauling a vacuum upstairs, digging in the garden - counts as resistance work too.

Is spicy food bad for you? For most people spicy food is perfectly healthy - chili peppers even bring vitamin C and antioxidants. Hot peppers irritate an existing ulcer or bad heartburn, but they do not create ulcers - bacteria and anti-inflammatory painkillers do that. The burning feeling comes from capsaicin, which trips heat sensors in your mouth but does not burn or damage the tissue.

What are head injury warning signs in children? Big cry, then back to normal play, is reassuring - but keep checking in over the next two days. Comfort them, offer a wrapped cold pack, and let them sleep if they settle - sleeping is fine as long as they rouse normally. Watch for 48 hours for repeated vomiting, unusual drowsiness or floppiness, irritability you cannot settle, unequal pupils, or any loss of consciousness. Babies under 1, falls from a significant height, or any of those warning signs mean the child should be seen by a doctor.

Why do kids have bad dreams? Nightmares are a normal part of childhood - most kids have them, especially between ages 3 and 8, often in the second half of the night. The best response is calm comfort: a hug, reassurance that it was a dream, and back to bed; keeping the room dim and settling quietly avoids fully waking them. Stressful events, scary shows and poor sleep raise nightmare frequency, so a steady routine helps.

When is dehydration serious? Urgent signs include no urination for 8 or more hours, sunken eyes, extreme thirst with inability to keep fluids down, marked lethargy or confusion, and cold, mottled hands and feet. Babies and older adults dehydrate faster and can deteriorate quickly, so they cross the urgent threshold sooner than healthy adults. In babies: dry diapers, a sunken soft spot and listlessness are the red flags to act on. Confusion in an older person during a vomiting illness is dehydration until a doctor says otherwise.

My friend is choking on a piece of steak but can still talk a little - what now? If they can cough, speak or breathe at all, encourage them to keep coughing - a strong cough often clears it on its own. Do not slap their back or try to remove the food while they are still coughing effectively, as you can push it deeper. Stay with them and watch whether the cough loses force. If the cough becomes silent or ineffective, or they cannot speak at all, move straight to back blows and abdominal thrusts.

How much exercise do children need? Children and teens need around 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity every day, and unlike adults they do not need it in one block - the day can be stitched together from play, sport, walking and chores. Several days a week should include activities that strengthen muscle and bone: climbing, jumping, running games, ball sports. Unstructured play counts fully, and for young children it is the primary recommendation. The most effective lever is adult modeling - kids move more in families that move, and limiting recreational screen time frees the hours to do it.

What does dehydrated pee look like? Thirst is the first signal, followed by a dry mouth, dark yellow urine, tiredness, headache and lightheadedness on standing. Pee color is the quickest check: pale straw is well hydrated, dark amber means you are behind. Dark amber urine is the single most practical daily hydration gauge. Older adults and young children feel thirst later, so they dehydrate faster and need watching in hot weather or during illness. By the time you feel thirsty you are already mildly behind - regular sips beat catch-up gulping.

What is the difference between a reliever and preventer inhaler? Reliever inhalers (usually blue) contain fast-acting medicine that opens the airways within minutes - they are the emergency tool. Preventer inhalers contain a low steroid dose taken every day whether or not you feel symptoms, because they work by calming the underlying inflammation. Needing the blue reliever three or more times a week is a sign the preventer routine needs adjusting. A spacer tube makes inhalers more effective - much more medicine reaches the lungs, especially in children - and a pharmacist or nurse can check your technique anytime.

My friend is having an asthma attack and the inhaler is not working - what now? Sit the person upright - do not lie them down - keep them calm, and help them take one puff of their reliever inhaler every 30 to 60 seconds, up to a maximum of 10 puffs. If there is no improvement after 10 puffs, or the person is getting worse, too breathless to speak in sentences, or turning pale or blue, call emergency services immediately. You can repeat the 10-puff cycle while waiting for the ambulance. An attack that needs more reliever than usual, or reliever that stops working as well as it used to, is a warning to get the asthma plan reviewed.

Why do we get fevers when we are sick? A fever is your immune system turning up body temperature to help fight infection - it is a response, not a disease. The number on the thermometer matters less than how the person looks and feels. Treating the discomfort with paracetamol or ibuprofen is reasonable; forcing a normal temperature is not required, and mild fevers may even help the immune response. How unwell someone seems - alertness, drinking, breathing - tells you more than the reading.

Do I need to wash hands after touching my phone? Wash your hands before preparing or eating food, after using the toilet, after coughing, sneezing or blowing your nose, and after touching pets or their waste. Also wash after handling garbage, after commuting on public transport, and before and around anyone who is ill. These moments are where germs actually travel onto your hands and then to your mouth, eyes and food.

What causes sudden dizziness? Brief lightheadedness on standing is usually a short blood-pressure dip, made more likely by dehydration, heat, hunger or certain medications. Vertigo - the sensation that you or the room is spinning - points to the inner ear, where the balance organs live. Sitting or lying down promptly prevents the dizziness from becoming a faint. Recurrent episodes, or dizziness on turning over in bed with brief spins, are worth describing to a doctor - the inner-ear causes are often very treatable. Stand up slowly after lying down, keep fluids up, and eat regularly - those three habits prevent most episodes.

Why does a double spirit count as 2 units? One unit is 10 ml of pure alcohol; a single 25 ml measure of spirits is 1 unit. A standard pint of lager carries roughly 2.5 units, so the 14-unit weekly limit is about 5-6 pints spread across the week. Because glass sizes and drink strengths vary, checking the label or a unit calculator beats guessing.

Why is my throat worse in the morning? The vast majority of sore throats are viral and clear within about a week on their own. Warm drinks with honey, rest, and paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain do more than most sprays and lozenges. Honey in a warm drink is cheap, safe (over age 1) and genuinely soothing. Dry indoor air and mouth-breathing at night make mornings worse - a humidifier or simply more fluids often helps.

Why did I go grey and wobbly standing in line? Most faints give a warning: sudden heat, a grey or pale face, ringing ears, dim vision and a cold sweat. The moment you feel it, lie down or sit with your head between your knees - fainting standing up is what causes head injuries. The feeling usually passes in under a minute once blood returns to the brain. Tell a doctor if it happens repeatedly, happens with chest pain or a racing heart, or occurs during exercise.

What about chemical or electrical burns? Get medical help for any burn larger than the person's palm, or on the face, hands, feet, genitals, or over a joint. White, leathery or charred-looking skin means a deep burn, and chemical or electrical burns always need professional assessment. Young children, babies and older adults should have most burns other than tiny ones assessed by a professional. While you wait, keep up the cool running water and cover the area loosely.

Do crash diets work? Lasting weight loss comes from a small, steady calorie gap: smaller portions, more fiber and protein, fewer sugary drinks and less alcohol, plus more daily movement. Around half a kilogram (about a pound) a week is a realistic pace, and slower losses are the ones that stick. Fad diets work briefly because they cut calories, but most people regain the weight when they stop - changes you can live with win.

How do I remove a splinter? Clean tweezers, steady pull along the entry angle, then wash - that is the whole job for most splinters. If it is buried under the skin, a sterilized needle can gently lift the skin over the end before you tweeze it out. Wash the area again afterward, cover it, and watch for redness or pus over the next few days. Do not dig aggressively; splinters that are deep, near the eye, or causing spreading redness belong with a doctor, and a deep dirty splinter may raise the tetanus question.

Should I drink water before meals? A glass of water before a meal adds a little stretch to your stomach, and some studies find people eat slightly less afterwards. Drinking with meals is fine and does not interfere with digestion - the 'water washes away stomach acid' idea is a myth. Water with food is harmless and can add to fullness; the 'bad for digestion' claim is a myth.

Should pregnant women eat fish? Aim for two portions of fish a week, and make one of them oily - each portion about 140 grams. The omega-3 fats in oily fish such as salmon, sardines and mackerel support your heart and brain. Pregnant women should keep oily fish to no more than two portions a week and avoid shark, swordfish and marlin because of mercury.

Does caffeine count from tea and chocolate in pregnancy? Pregnant women are advised to keep caffeine under 200 mg a day - about 2 mugs of instant coffee or one strong filter coffee. Too much caffeine during pregnancy is linked with low birth weight, which is why the 200 mg cap exists. Remember to count tea, cola, energy drinks and chocolate towards the daily total.

Which allergy medicine will not make me sleepy? Antihistamines block the histamine that causes sneezing, itching, runny nose and hives, so they ease symptoms rather than cure the allergy. Newer formulations (cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine style) cause little drowsiness for most people, while older ones do - which is why the older type is now mostly a bedtime option. Starting them before or at the very start of allergy season usually works better than chasing symptoms. If antihistamines alone are not enough, steroid nasal sprays are the standard next step - a pharmacist can walk you through it.

Is sitting all day bad for you even if I exercise? Exercise does not fully offset 10 motionless hours; the breaks between sitting do real work. Standing or moving briefly every 30 to 60 minutes - a lap of the room, a few stairs, a 2-minute stretch - measurably improves blood sugar and circulation. A standing desk helps, but alternating positions beats standing motionless for hours. The practical pattern is exercise plus frequent breaks: the two protect different systems.

Should I replace my toothbrush after being sick? Replace your toothbrush - or electric brush head - about every 3 months. Change it sooner if the bristles splay or fray, because a worn brush cleans far worse. Many people also swap it after an illness like strep throat, as a cheap precaution.

How long is too long to be constipated? See a doctor if constipation has lasted more than about 3 weeks despite fiber and fluids, or if it keeps returning. Blood in the stool, unexplained weight loss, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or constipation alternating with diarrhea need assessment rather than self-treatment. A new, persistent change in bowel habit - especially over 50 - is something doctors always want to hear about. Bright red streaks on paper from a straining-related fissure are common and usually minor, but any bleeding deserves at least a mention at an appointment.

Are protein bars and cereals ultra-processed? Ultra-processed foods are industrial products built from refined ingredients plus additives you would not find in a home kitchen - think sodas, candy, packaged cookies, instant noodles and many ready meals. Studies link diets high in them with weight gain and higher rates of several diseases, though the research is still developing. 'Processed' is not automatically bad - frozen vegetables, canned beans, wholegrain bread and plain yogurt are processed too, and they are healthy staples. A practical rule: cook from basic ingredients most of the time and treat ultra-processed food as an occasional convenience.

Are OTC cough syrups worth buying? For adults and children over 1, studies suggest honey is about as effective as - and often better than - over-the-counter cough syrups at easing cough, particularly night-time symptoms. A spoonful of honey, or honey stirred into a warm (not boiling) drink, is cheap and low-risk; never give honey to babies under 1 because of infant botulism risk. Many OTC syrups have thin evidence for benefit, and combination products carry dosing-confusion risks. Warmth, moisture and honey address the irritated airway directly, which is where most cough medicine evidence points.

Should I avoid egg yolks? For most healthy people, eggs are a nutritious food and there is no set limit - an egg a day fits comfortably in a healthy diet. The cholesterol you eat affects blood cholesterol far less than saturated fat does, though a few 'high responders' see bigger rises. If you have familial high cholesterol, heart disease or diabetes, ask your doctor what suits you. Eggs bring protein, vitamins and minerals for relatively few calories, so they earn their place on the plate.

How many baby carrots make one portion? One portion is about 80 grams, which is roughly what fits in your hand. A medium apple or banana, three heaped spoons of veg, or a dessert bowl of salad each count as one portion. Dried fruit counts too, but only 30 grams - about a tablespoon of raisins - because it is sticky, sugary and easy to overeat. Juice and smoothies can only ever count as one portion a day, however much you drink.

Do you need to stretch after a workout? Finish hard sessions with a few minutes of progressively lighter movement - jogging becomes walking becomes easy strolling. This keeps blood moving back to the heart while demand drops, which reduces the light-headedness of an abrupt stop. A cool-down is a good window for static stretching, when muscles are warm and pliable. Five minutes is plenty for most moderate sessions; the harder the session, the longer the taper.

Is athlete's foot contagious? Athlete's foot is a fungal infection that makes the skin between the toes itchy, scaly, red and sometimes cracked. Over-the-counter antifungal creams work well if you keep using them for the full course - usually 1 to 2 weeks after the skin looks better - or it returns. It spreads through damp floors and shared towels, so dry feet well, change socks daily, and don't share footwear.

Dizziness with chest pain - what should I do? Call emergency services if dizziness comes with chest pain, palpitations, new weakness or numbness, slurred speech, severe headache, or double vision - these can signal heart or brain problems. See a doctor promptly for dizziness that keeps recurring, lasts continuously for hours, or comes with new hearing loss in one ear. Dizziness from standing too fast in a warm room is usually benign; dizziness that arrives with neurological signs never gets the benign assumption. If dizziness has already caused faints, describe those events to a doctor rather than only the dizziness.

Should I snack between meals? Good snack choices pair protein or fiber: fruit with nuts, plain yogurt, hummus with vegetables, or wholegrain crackers with cheese. Constant sugary snacking keeps teeth bathed in acid and makes energy swing through the day. If afternoon cravings hit, check the basics first: a proper lunch with protein and enough water prevents many 'hunger' episodes.

How many steps a day is actually enough? The 10,000-step figure traces back to a 1960s Japanese pedometer campaign, not to physiology. Large studies find steep health benefits up to around 7,000 to 8,000 steps a day, with further but smaller gains beyond. Roughly 7,000-8,000 steps captures a large share of the health benefit for most adults. Step trackers motivate, but treat their goals as tools, not verdicts.

Why do I crave junk food when I am tired? After short sleep, hunger hormones tilt toward eating more, and cravings lean toward sugary, high-calorie food. Tired brains also reach for quick, sugary energy and have weaker brakes on impulse snacking. Studies consistently link chronic short sleep with higher rates of weight gain, though sleep alone is not the whole story.

How many nuts should I eat a day? Nuts are packed with unsaturated fats, protein, fiber, vitamin E and minerals. A small handful a day - about 30 grams - is a sensible portion, and studies find nut eaters do not tend to gain weight from them, probably because they are so filling. Choose unsalted versions, and plain over honey-coated or heavily roasted.

When should I apply deodorant? Deodorant covers odor with fragrance and antibacterials; antiperspirant actually reduces sweating by briefly plugging sweat ducts with aluminum salts. Claims linking antiperspirant ingredients to cancer have been tested and do not hold up; the safety record is long and clean. Apply either to clean, dry skin at night for many products works best, since you sweat less then and the active ingredients hold better.

Do white spots on tonsils mean I need antibiotics? Features that suggest a bacterial (strep) throat are a sudden high fever, swollen and tender glands in the neck, white or pus-coated tonsils, and notably no cough. White tonsil patches alone are not conclusive, but combined with fever and no cough they warrant a check. Doctors use these signs (sometimes with a rapid swab) to decide about antibiotics rather than handing them out for every red throat. Untreated strep can occasionally lead to complications, which is why a bacterial-pattern throat deserves a real assessment.

When should a headache after hitting my head worry me? A headache that explodes to 'worst of my life' intensity within seconds needs emergency assessment - it can signal bleeding around the brain. Headache with fever and a stiff neck, headache with new weakness, slurred speech, confusion or vision loss, and headache after a head injury are also emergencies. A new, different headache in someone over 50, or one that wakes you nightly, deserves prompt medical review rather than self-care. Everything else - band-like, gradual, with clear stress or dehydration triggers - is usually manageable with the basics.

What is a healthy amount of red meat? Red meat such as beef, lamb and pork supplies protein and iron, but many people eat more of it than they need. If you eat more than about 90 grams of red or processed meat a day, guidance suggests cutting down towards 70 grams. Simple swaps make that easy: a couple of meat-free days a week, chicken or fish some nights, or smaller portions.

What does the traffic light label mean? Start with the ingredients list, which runs from the biggest component to the smallest - if sugar or fat appears near the top, the food is mostly that. Comparing per 100 g is the fair way to judge two products, since serving sizes vary by brand. Traffic-light labels give a quick read: lots of reds for fat, salt or sugar means go easy.

Why do doctors keep telling me to eat more fiber? Fiber keeps your digestion regular and helps prevent constipation. It also feeds the healthy bacteria in your gut, helps you feel full after meals, and can lower cholesterol. Diets rich in fiber are linked with a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer.

What is the fastest way to heal a blister? Resist popping it; the fluid is sterile and the skin over it does the job of a dressing. Cover it with a soft plaster or a donut-shaped pad that takes pressure off the blister itself. If it bursts on its own, wash gently with clean water, keep the flap of skin in place, and cover with a clean dressing. See a doctor if it fills with yellow-green pus, the surrounding skin turns hot and spreading-red, or you have diabetes and blisters on your feet.

Why do I always overeat at dinner? Simple tricks help: use a smaller plate, serve food in the kitchen instead of from the table, and stash leftovers before you sit down. Eat slowly and pause partway through - your brain needs about 20 minutes to register fullness. Protein and fiber make meals more filling, so you are less likely to go back for seconds.

Why is drying between my toes important? Fungus thrives in warm, damp, dark places - exactly what sweaty, enclosed toes provide when left damp. Change socks daily - more often if they get damp - and rotate shoes so each pair dries out for a day or two between wears. In shared showers and locker rooms, flip-flops cut the risk of picking up athlete's foot.

Which fats are healthy? Your body needs some fat, and the type matters: unsaturated fats - olive and rapeseed oil, nuts, seeds, oily fish - support heart health. Saturated fats - butter, ghee, coconut oil, fatty processed meat and pastry - raise cholesterol, so keep them to a smaller share of your diet. The smartest move is usually to swap rather than add: replace butter with olive oil instead of pouring oil over everything.

How do I stay hydrated with a stomach bug? Mouthfuls every few minutes beat big drinks; rehydration solution is the ideal fluid when losses are heavy. Eat as tolerated once vomiting settles; the old 'brat diet only' advice has given way to just eating what you can keep down. Seek medical care for signs of dehydration (dizziness, no urine for 8 hours, sunken eyes), blood in vomit or stool, severe abdominal pain, or symptoms lasting beyond a few days. Babies, elderly relatives and pregnant women should be checked earlier in the course.

Is coughing good for you? A cough is the airways' clearing mechanism: it expels mucus, dust and irritants, protecting the lungs. A chesty (productive) cough moves phlegm up and out, while a dry cough is irritation without much to clear - which is why the two are treated differently. The post-cold cough can run 2 to 3 weeks without meaning anything new is wrong. Suppressants can help a dry cough disturb sleep less, but stopping a productive cough entirely can trap mucus. Steam, warm fluids and honey (over age 1) soothe the irritated airway better than most bottles on the shelf.

Should towels be washed hot? Wash bath towels after about 3 uses and hand towels more often; when someone is ill, give them their own and wash everything hot. Weekly-hot washing of bedding also kills the dust mites that allergy sufferers react to. Damp towels turn smelly fast because bacteria multiply in the folds; hang them spread out to dry, not crumpled on a hook.

How many grams of added sugar is too much? For adults, guidance is to keep added sugar below about 30 grams a day - roughly 7 sugar cubes. Children should have less: no more than about 6 cubes a day for ages 7 to 10, and less again for younger kids. It is 'free sugars' that count against the limit: the kind added to products, plus honey, syrups and juice. Whole fruit and plain milk do not count. Most free sugars hide in soda, candy, cookies, sweetened cereal and sauces rather than the sugar bowl.

Should I pee on a jellyfish sting? Seawater rinse, gentle tentacle removal and a hot-water soak are the mainstream steps. Remove any tentacles with tweezers or a gloved hand, without rubbing the skin. Soaking in hot (not scalding) water for 20 to 45 minutes eases the pain for most stings. Vinegar helps certain tropical species like box jellyfish but can worsen others, so follow local beach guidance where you swim.

How often should you wash your hair? Most people do not need a full shower every day; washing every 2 to 3 days keeps most skin healthy, with a daily wash of armpits, groin, feet and hands. If you do shower daily, keep it short and lukewarm, and moisturize afterwards to replace what the water washes away. Wash hair when it feels greasy or looks it - for most people that is every few days, not every day.

Should I take medicine for a cold? Rest, fluids and simple painkillers are the evidence-backed core of cold care. Saline rinses, steamy showers and honey in warm water (adults and children over 1) each ease specific symptoms. Vitamin C has not been shown to shorten a cold once it has started. Combination cold products often mix the same ingredients, so check labels to avoid double-dosing.

Do crash diets work? Lasting weight loss comes from a small, steady calorie gap: smaller portions, more fiber and protein, fewer sugary drinks and less alcohol, plus more daily movement. Around half a kilogram (about a pound) a week is a realistic pace, and slower losses are the ones that stick. Fad diets work briefly because they cut calories, but most people regain the weight when they stop - changes you can live with win. If you have a lot of weight to lose or other health conditions, a doctor or dietitian can tailor a plan.

My cut is still bleeding after 20 minutes of pressure - what now? Get medical help for cuts that are deep, gaping, longer than a couple of centimeters, or that keep bleeding after 10 to 20 minutes of firm pressure. Pad around anything stuck in a wound and leave it for the professionals to remove. Animal and human bites, dirty rusty wounds (for a tetanus check), and cuts with numbness beyond them also deserve professional care. Growing redness, warmth, swelling, pus or red streaks toward the heart in the following days are signs of infection.

How do I start exercising after years of being sedentary? Start below what feels like your limit and increase gradually - roughly 10 percent more per week is a safe pace for most people. Walking is the best re-entry activity: self-paced, joint-friendly, and easy to measure. Chest pain, dizziness or pain that alters your gait are all stop-and-check signals, not badges of effort. Talk to a doctor first if you have heart disease symptoms, uncontrolled blood pressure, diabetes complications, or joint problems - for most people, starting gentle exercise is safer than not starting. Consistency at a modest level beats heroic starts that end in injury by week three.

How much do newborns sleep? Newborns sleep 14 to 17 hours a day, but in short stretches of 2 to 4 hours because their tiny stomachs need frequent feeding. Night waking in young babies is developmental, not a problem to fix - feeding needs and immature body clocks drive it. Parents cope best by sleeping when the baby sleeps, taking shifts, and asking for help.

Does a higher fever mean a worse illness? A fever is your immune system turning up body temperature to help fight infection - it is a response, not a disease. The number on the thermometer matters less than how the person looks and feels. Treating the discomfort with paracetamol or ibuprofen is reasonable; forcing a normal temperature is not required, and mild fevers may even help the immune response. How unwell someone seems - alertness, drinking, breathing - tells you more than the reading. A temperature of about 38C (100.4F) or higher counts as a fever when measured properly.
